Diagram: CCR Control Schematic

Case Study: Division 25 — Field Case Study Troubleshooting (cross-reference where applicable)

Rev 0 — Initial issue
CCR-091 CCR Wrong Current Indication

Symptom — The output current value shown on the CCR's local display and/or reported to the PLC/ALCMS does not match the actual output current as independently measured, even though the CCR's actual regulation behaviour may be correct.

Equipment / System

CCR current feedback sensor, controller current measurement/scaling logic, and current value indication outputs (local display and remote data point).

Possible Causes
HighCurrent feedback sensor drifted out of calibration, reporting a systematically incorrect value
HighController current scaling/conversion parameter incorrectly configured, offsetting an otherwise accurate raw sensor reading
MediumCurrent feedback sensor wiring loose, corroded, or picking up electrical noise, producing an inaccurate reading
MediumCommunication data scaling mismatch between the controller and PLC/ALCMS, correct at the controller but wrong once transmitted
LowerLocal display and remote current value disagree with each other, indicating the fault is isolated to one indication path
Required Tools
True-RMS clamp meter (calibrated reference)MultimeterCCR configuration/parameter toolManufacturer alarm/parameter code reference
Safety Precautions
  • Apply LOTO before inspecting current feedback sensor wiring.
  • Do not adjust the actual output current setpoint in an attempt to "correct" a display reading — confirm which value is actually wrong first.
Diagnostic Procedure
  1. ObservationIndependently and simultaneously measure the actual output current using a calibrated reference clamp meter at the series circuit.
  2. ObservationCompare the independently measured value against what is shown on the local display and separately reported to the PLC/ALCMS.
  3. DecisionIndependent measurement confirms the displayed/reported value is wrong → sensor, scaling, or wiring fault, proceed to isolate. Independent measurement confirms the displayed value is actually correct → no fault in current indication; investigate the original complaint further.
  4. MeasurementCheck the current feedback sensor's calibration against manufacturer reference values.
  5. MeasurementInspect current feedback sensor wiring for looseness, corrosion, or noise pickup.
  6. MeasurementVerify the controller's current scaling/conversion parameter and, separately, the communication data scaling used when reporting to the PLC/ALCMS.
  7. DecisionLocal display and remote value disagree with each other → isolated to the communication/scaling path for whichever indication is wrong.
  8. Fault LocationIsolate to the current feedback sensor, its wiring, the controller scaling parameter, or the communication scaling.
  9. Root CauseConfirm the specific cause by correcting it and re-verifying against the independent reference measurement.
Test Points
Actual output current (calibrated reference measurement)
Local display current value
Remote (PLC/ALCMS) current value
Current feedback sensor calibration and wiring
Controller and communication current scaling parameters
Root Cause Verification

After correction, verify the local display, remote reported value, and independently measured actual current all agree across the full intensity step range.

Corrective Action
  • Recalibrate or replace the drifted current feedback sensor.
  • Correct the controller current scaling/conversion parameter.
  • Repair the current feedback sensor wiring.
  • Correct the communication data scaling configuration.
Preventive Action
  • Include current feedback sensor calibration checks in the annual PM.
  • Document and version-control scaling/conversion parameters at both the controller and PLC/ALCMS.
  • Cross-check displayed/reported current against a reference measurement periodically, not only when a discrepancy is suspected.
Related References

SOP: SOP-CCR-02 (CCR Output Verification), SOP-CCR-10 (Protection Relay Calibration)

Standards: —

Diagram: CCR Control Schematic

Case Study: Division 25 — Field Case Study Troubleshooting (cross-reference where applicable)

Rev 0 — Initial issue
CCR-092 CCR Wrong Step Indication

Symptom — The intensity step shown on the CCR's local display and/or reported to the PLC/ALCMS does not match the actual intensity step the CCR is regulating to, even though the actual light output/current level may be correct for the step it is truly on.

Equipment / System

CCR intensity step selection logic, step feedback/readback path, and step value indication outputs (local display and remote data point).

Possible Causes
HighStep command received correctly and actioned correctly by the regulator, but the step readback/feedback value used for indication is wrong
HighStep selection logic itself has actioned the wrong step while reporting the originally commanded step, so displayed step matches command but not actual output
MediumStep value data mapping/scaling error between the controller and PLC/ALCMS, correct at the controller but wrong once transmitted
MediumStale/cached step value not updating promptly after a genuine step change
LowerLocal display and remote step value disagree with each other, indicating the fault is isolated to one indication path
Required Tools
True-RMS clamp meter (calibrated reference)CCR configuration/parameter toolManufacturer alarm/parameter code referenceCCR step/intensity chart
Safety Precautions
  • Apply LOTO before internal inspection if step selection wiring/relays need to be accessed.
  • Confirm actual light output/current independently before relying on displayed step for operational decisions.
Diagnostic Procedure
  1. ObservationIndependently measure actual output current and compare against the manufacturer's step/current chart to determine which step the CCR is genuinely regulating to.
  2. ObservationCompare the independently determined actual step against what is shown on the local display and separately reported to the PLC/ALCMS.
  3. DecisionActual step (from measured current) disagrees with both indications → the step selection/regulation itself may be at fault, investigate as an output/step fault rather than an indication fault. Actual step matches actual output but disagrees with one or both indications → genuine indication-only fault, proceed to isolate.
  4. MeasurementCommand a known step change and observe whether the step readback/feedback value updates promptly and correctly at both the controller and remote.
  5. MeasurementVerify step value data mapping/scaling configuration between the controller and PLC/ALCMS.
  6. Fault LocationIsolate to the step readback/feedback path, the communication data mapping, or a stale-value update issue.
  7. Root CauseConfirm the specific cause by commanding several step changes and verifying prompt, correct indication each time.
Test Points
Actual output current vs. manufacturer step/current chart
Local display step value
Remote (PLC/ALCMS) step value
Step readback/feedback update timing
Step value data mapping/scaling configuration
Root Cause Verification

After correction, command a full sequence of step changes and confirm the local display, remote reported step, and independently verified actual step all agree promptly at each step.

Corrective Action
  • Correct the step readback/feedback path fault.
  • Correct the communication data mapping/scaling for the step value.
  • Address a stale-value update issue per manufacturer firmware/configuration guidance.
  • If the underlying fault is in step selection/regulation itself, investigate per the relevant Division 03 (Intensity Control) topic.
Preventive Action
  • Include step indication verification (command vs. actual vs. displayed/reported) in the routine PM.
  • Document and version-control step value data mapping between the controller and PLC/ALCMS.
  • Verify step readback update timing during commissioning and after any firmware update.
Related References

SOP: SOP-CCR-03 (CCR Intensity Step Verification)

Standards: —

Diagram: CCR Control Schematic

Case Study: Division 25 — Field Case Study Troubleshooting (cross-reference where applicable)

Rev 0 — Initial issue
CCR-093 CCR Alarm Status Not Updating

Symptom — An active CCR alarm/fault condition is not reflected, or a cleared alarm remains shown as active, on the local display and/or at the PLC/ALCMS — the alarm status indication is stale rather than reflecting the controller's current alarm state.

Equipment / System

CCR controller alarm logic, alarm status indication outputs (local display and remote data point), and event/alarm log.

Possible Causes
HighAlarm status data point not updating/refreshing correctly in the communication path to the PLC/ALCMS
HighLocal display alarm indicator logic fault, independent of the controller's actual internal alarm state
MediumAlarm requires a manual acknowledgement/reset step that has not been performed, so it correctly remains shown as active per design, and is not actually a fault
MediumController's internal alarm state itself stuck/latched due to a logic fault, distinct from the indication path
LowerAlarm status data mapping/point configuration error at the PLC/ALCMS, showing an unrelated or incorrect alarm point
Required Tools
Manufacturer diagnostic/configuration toolCommunication link test equipment (per protocol)CCR event/alarm log export toolCCR control schematic
Safety Precautions
  • Treat an unclear alarm status as potentially real until proven otherwise — do not assume an alarm is stale/incorrect without verifying the controller's actual internal state.
  • Apply LOTO before internal inspection where required.
Diagnostic Procedure
  1. ObservationQuery the controller's actual current internal alarm state directly (via its own diagnostic interface/event log), independent of what is shown on the display or at the PLC/ALCMS.
  2. DecisionController's actual internal state matches what is shown → no fault in indication; the alarm is genuinely active (or genuinely clear) as displayed. Controller's actual internal state disagrees with what is displayed/reported → indication fault, proceed to isolate.
  3. ObservationCheck whether the alarm design requires a manual acknowledgement/reset step per manufacturer documentation, which would explain a persistently "active" display that is not itself a fault.
  4. MeasurementWhere indication disagrees with actual state, verify the alarm status data point mapping/configuration between the controller and PLC/ALCMS.
  5. MeasurementCheck the local display's alarm indicator logic independently of the remote indication path.
  6. Fault LocationIsolate to the communication data mapping, the local display alarm logic, or a manual acknowledgement step that has simply not been performed.
  7. Root CauseConfirm the specific cause by resolving it and re-verifying alarm indication matches actual controller state through a test alarm cycle where safely possible.
Test Points
Controller's actual internal alarm state (direct query)
Local display alarm indicator
Remote (PLC/ALCMS) alarm status point
Alarm acknowledgement/reset requirement per manufacturer documentation
Alarm status data point mapping/configuration
Root Cause Verification

After correction, where safely possible, trigger and clear a test alarm condition and confirm the local display and remote status both promptly and correctly reflect the change.

Corrective Action
  • Correct the alarm status data point mapping/configuration.
  • Repair the local display alarm indicator logic.
  • Perform the required manual acknowledgement/reset if that was the actual cause, and document the procedure for operators.
  • Address the controller's internal alarm logic fault if confirmed, up to controller replacement if required (see CCR-079).
Preventive Action
  • Include alarm indication verification (controller state vs. displayed/reported state) in the routine PM.
  • Document alarm acknowledgement/reset requirements clearly for site operators.
  • Document and version-control alarm status data point mapping.
Related References

SOP: SOP-CCR-10 (Protection Relay Calibration), SOP-CCR-12 (CCR–ALCMS Communication Verification)

Standards: —

Diagram: CCR Protection Schematic

Rev 0 — Initial issue
CCR-094 CCR Remote Feedback Missing

Symptom — One or more expected feedback data points (status, current, step, alarm, or other telemetry) from the CCR are entirely absent at the PLC/ALCMS — not merely wrong, but not present or updating at all — while the communication link itself may otherwise appear healthy.

Equipment / System

CCR controller data point configuration, communication interface, and PLC/ALCMS point database/configuration.

Possible Causes
HighThe specific data point was never configured or was removed from the CCR controller's communication mapping
HighThe specific data point was never configured or was removed from the PLC/ALCMS point database
MediumCommunication link is healthy overall but the specific point's polling/subscription is not active
MediumA firmware update at the CCR controller changed or reset the data point mapping without corresponding update at the PLC/ALCMS
LowerThe feedback source itself (sensor/logic) generating that specific data point has failed, so there is genuinely nothing to report (see the relevant specific topic, e.g. CCR-090/091/092)
Required Tools
Manufacturer diagnostic/configuration toolCommunication link test equipment (per protocol)Communication point mapping documentationCCR control schematic
Safety Precautions
  • Apply LOTO before internal inspection where required.
Diagnostic Procedure
  1. ObservationConfirm overall communication link health (see CCR-087/088/089) to rule out a total link failure as the cause of the missing point.
  2. ObservationIdentify precisely which data point(s) are missing versus which are present and updating correctly.
  3. MeasurementCheck the CCR controller's communication point mapping configuration for the presence and correct configuration of the missing point.
  4. MeasurementCheck the PLC/ALCMS point database/configuration for the presence and correct configuration of the same point.
  5. DecisionPoint missing from the CCR controller's mapping → controller-side configuration fault. Point present at the controller but missing from the PLC/ALCMS database → PLC/ALCMS-side configuration fault. Point present and correctly configured at both ends but still not updating → investigate the underlying feedback source per the relevant specific topic.
  6. Fault LocationIsolate to the controller-side mapping, the PLC/ALCMS-side database, or the underlying feedback source.
  7. Root CauseConfirm the specific cause by adding/correcting the missing configuration and verifying the point begins reporting correctly.
Test Points
Overall communication link health
CCR controller point mapping configuration
PLC/ALCMS point database configuration
Underlying feedback source for the missing point
Root Cause Verification

After correction, confirm the previously missing data point reports correctly and updates promptly through a sustained monitoring period.

Corrective Action
  • Add or correct the missing point in the CCR controller's communication mapping.
  • Add or correct the missing point in the PLC/ALCMS point database/configuration.
  • Activate polling/subscription for the specific point if that was the cause.
  • Address the underlying feedback source fault per the relevant specific topic if the point itself has no valid data to report.
Preventive Action
  • Maintain a current, version-controlled point mapping document covering both the CCR controller and PLC/ALCMS.
  • Re-verify point mapping after any firmware update at the CCR controller.
  • Include a full data point inventory check in the routine PM.
Related References

SOP: SOP-CCR-12 (CCR–ALCMS Communication Verification)

Diagram: CCR Communication Architecture Diagram

Case Study: Division 25 — Field Case Study Troubleshooting (cross-reference where applicable)

Rev 0 — Initial issue
CCR-095 CCR Data Communication Failure

Symptom — A general, unresolved data communication fault affecting the CCR that does not clearly fit a single specific topic (link down, incorrect values, missing points, or intermittent behaviour observed together or in an ambiguous combination), requiring a broader systematic investigation across the full communication chain.

Equipment / System

CCR controller communication interface, communication link/network, any intermediate PLC/RTU, and the PLC/ALCMS-side interface — the full communication chain end to end.

Possible Causes
HighA single root cause manifesting as multiple symptoms across the chain (e.g. a marginal link causing both intermittent dropouts and occasional data corruption)
HighMultiple independent faults coinciding across different points in the chain, making the overall picture appear more complex than any single specific topic covers
MediumA recent change (firmware update, network change, configuration change) affecting communication behaviour in a way not yet isolated to a specific point
MediumAn intermittent or environmental factor (power quality, EMI, temperature) affecting communication hardware broadly rather than one specific component
LowerThe issue is actually several distinct, already-covered faults occurring close together in time and has not yet been separated into its component parts
Required Tools
Communication link test equipment (per protocol)Data logger for trend/repeated-event analysisManufacturer diagnostic/configuration toolCommunication architecture diagramChange/maintenance log
Safety Precautions
  • Apply LOTO before physical inspection of any communication wiring.
  • Coordinate with the ALCMS/control room and any other stakeholders before broad testing that could affect other monitored equipment.
Diagnostic Procedure
  1. ObservationSystematically document every distinct symptom observed (dropouts, wrong values, missing points, timing) with timestamps, to determine whether this is one root cause or several coinciding faults.
  2. ObservationReview the change/maintenance log for any recent firmware, network, or configuration change coinciding with the onset of symptoms.
  3. DecisionSymptoms trace to a single identifiable point or cause → re-route the investigation to the matching specific topic (CCR-087 through CCR-094) for detailed diagnosis. Symptoms genuinely span multiple independent points → proceed with a full end-to-end systematic check.
  4. MeasurementWhere a full systematic check is needed, verify each segment of the communication chain in turn — CCR controller interface, link/network, intermediate PLC/RTU, and PLC/ALCMS interface — checking status and configuration at each.
  5. MeasurementCross-reference findings against any recent change identified in the maintenance log.
  6. Fault LocationIsolate each contributing fault to its specific point in the chain, treating multiple faults separately rather than seeking one all-encompassing cause if the evidence does not support it.
  7. Root CauseConfirm each identified cause independently and verify the chain is fully healthy end to end before closing out.
Test Points
Full communication chain, segment by segment (CCR controller, link/network, intermediate PLC/RTU, PLC/ALCMS interface)
Change/maintenance log for recent relevant changes
Environmental factors (power quality, EMI, temperature) at communication hardware locations
Root Cause Verification

After all identified faults are resolved, monitor the full communication chain through a sustained multi-day period covering representative operating and environmental conditions, and confirm no recurrence of any of the originally observed symptoms.

Corrective Action
  • Apply the specific corrective action for each fault once isolated to a specific point in the chain, per the matching specific topic where applicable.
  • Revert or correct a recent change confirmed as the cause.
  • Address environmental factors (power quality, EMI, temperature protection) if confirmed as a contributing cause.
Preventive Action
  • Maintain a detailed, timestamped change/maintenance log covering firmware, network, and configuration changes.
  • Include full end-to-end communication chain verification in periodic (not just reactive) maintenance.
  • Encourage systematic symptom documentation before broad troubleshooting begins, to catch multi-fault situations early.
Related References

SOP: SOP-CCR-06 (Repeated Fault Investigation Procedure), SOP-CCR-12 (CCR–ALCMS Communication Verification)

Frequently Asked Questions

Quick answers about CCR troubleshooting in the AGL Troubleshooting Atlas.

Q1What does Division 01 of the AGL Troubleshooting Atlas cover?

Division 01 is the CCR (Constant Current Regulator) troubleshooting reference. It publishes 95 diagnostic topics, CCR-001 to CCR-095, across six subsections: Start-Up & Power (20), CCR Output (20), Intensity Control (15), Protection & Alarms (15), Cooling & Internal Components (10) and Monitoring & Communication (15).

Q2What is a CCR in airfield ground lighting?

A constant current regulator (CCR) is the series-circuit lighting control unit that feeds airfield lights with a regulated current and sets their brightness through intensity steps. The reference records describe CCRs as thyristor- or IGBT-regulated units rated about 4-100 kW with 6.6 A output (20 A or 30 A on legacy systems) and 5-step or stepless intensity control.

Q3What information does each CCR troubleshooting topic include?

Every topic follows the same 11-field diagnostic record: the symptom, equipment/system, possible causes ranked by likelihood (high, medium or low), required tools, safety precautions, diagnostic procedure, test points, root cause verification, corrective action, preventive action and related references (SOPs, standards, diagrams and case studies).

Q4What should I check first when a CCR will not start?

Start at the front panel or HMI: note whether the power-on lamp is lit and record the exact status and any alarm code before touching anything. Then work through the start-up topics (CCR-001 to CCR-020). High-probability causes for a CCR that will not start include an active emergency stop or a door interlock that is open or misaligned.

Q5What safety precautions apply before working on a CCR?

CCR output can reach several kV under load, depending on circuit length, so never work on the output terminals while the CCR is running or its capacitors are charged. Apply lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) on the CCR input isolator before any internal work. The related procedure is SOP-CCR-04 (CCR Isolation & LOTO Procedure).

Q6Which topics cover output current and output voltage faults?

CCR-021 to CCR-040 cover zero, low, high, unstable and fluctuating output current, current not matching the selected step, abnormal or unstable output voltage, no output despite healthy input, output dropping under load, hunting, overshoot, undershoot, regulation failure, output transformer overheating and internal output connection failure.

Q7How do I troubleshoot a missing or incorrect brightness step?

Use CCR-041 to CCR-055. They cover Brightness Steps 1 to 5 not working, one or multiple steps missing, incorrect or automatic intensity selection, commands not accepted, local and remote intensity control failure, incorrect step indication, step relay failure and a sticking intensity control relay. Related procedures include SOP-CCR-03 (Intensity Step Verification) and SOP-CCR-08 (Intensity Step Commissioning).

Q8Which CCR protection alarms are covered?

CCR-056 to CCR-070 cover earth fault, overcurrent, overvoltage, undervoltage, overtemperature, transformer temperature, door interlock, surge protection, internal fault, communication, fan failure and cooling failure alarms, plus protection relay failure, false alarms and repeated protection trips.

Q9How are CCR communication and ALCMS faults handled?

CCR-085 to CCR-095 cover local and remote control failure, PLC and ALCMS communication failure, intermittent communication, wrong status, current or step indication, alarm status not updating, missing remote feedback and data communication failure. Related procedures include SOP-CCR-11 (Communication Link Testing) and SOP-CCR-12 (CCR-ALCMS Communication Verification).

Q10Which standards does the CCR troubleshooting content reference?

Where a standard applies, it is cited in each topic's Related References. Examples include ICAO Annex 14 Volume I, FAA AC 150/5345-10, IEC 61820-3-2, IEC 60364, IEC 60204-1, IEC 60947-4-1, IEC 61643 and IEC 62305, and Indian Standards such as IS 7785 and IS 12290.
